items.title: Anthropic maps multi-agent failure modes
items.oneliner: Anthropic says AI-to-AI interactions may soon dominate, making coordination bugs and emergent failures a near-term engineering problem.

items.title: LittleLearner exposes training data limits
items.oneliner: A K-5-only LLM improved in-domain but failed out-of-scope, a clean reminder that scaling cannot invent missing knowledge.

items.title: AI helped port legacy weather code
items.oneliner: Researchers used AI to port 250,000 lines of Fortran to GPUs, then still needed rigorous validation for a 5.1x speedup.

items.title: PyPI still lacks reproducible builds
items.oneliner: PyPI reproducible builds remain unfinished, leaving Python packages harder to verify against tampering in the software supply chain.

items.title: Germany faces backlash over car telemetry
items.oneliner: German intelligence reform could widen access to vehicle telemetry, pushing connected-car data squarely into the surveillance debate.

items.title: PayPal's unlocked-screen lesson still lands
items.oneliner: A simple unlocked-screen prank taught identity risk better than compliance slides, which is still true for security training.

items.title: DuckDB is moving to async I/O
items.oneliner: DuckDB 2.0 adds asynchronous I/O for remote data, attacking the idle-thread bottleneck that cloud analytics keeps hitting.

items.title: Numba finally runs inside JupyterLite
items.oneliner: Numba in the browser delivered up to 249x speedups, making serverless scientific notebooks much more than a demo.

items.title: Comma opened its eGPU dock firmware
items.oneliner: Comma's Chestnut eGPU dock ships with open firmware, a rare hardware move that gives developers real control and debuggability.

items.title: Hermes agents get Grafana observability
items.oneliner: A new Grafana plugin traces LLM calls and tool executions, bringing agent debugging closer to normal production engineering.
